newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Egypt extradites suspected arsonist to Bahrain.
newsitem.headline: Egypt extradites suspected arsonist to Bahrain.

text.p: Egypt has extradited to Bahrain a fugitive Shi'ite Moslem accused of involvement in a deadly arson attack in the Gulf Arab state in July, a government official said on Tuesday.
"Egypt has extradited the man. He is currently in Bahrain and will be tried in court soon," the official told Reuters.
The official said Bahraini national Ibrahim Ahmed had been arrested in the northern Egyptian port city of Alexandria and later extradited following a Bahraini request.
Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Khalifa al-Khalifa has sent a cable of thanks to his Egyptian counterpart Hassan el-Alfy for extraditing Ahmed, Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency said.
"This (extradition) reflects security and judicial cooperation between brotherly Arabs...to maintain security and stability of all Arab countries," the agency said.
Ahmed was accused of involvement in an arson attack on a cold store in the small island of Sitra, linked with the capital Manama by a three-km (1.8-mile) causeway, in which two Asian workers died.

It was the first time Egypt had officially extradited a fugitive Bahraini since anti-government protests erupted in December 1994 by the island's majority Shi'ite community to press for economic and political reforms.
Six Asians were killed in June and July in two separate arson attacks believed related to the unrest. Seven Bangladeshi workers died in a blaze in 1996.
